Dyslexia is something that's been misrepresented, sometimes by experts. There is a conditions which used to be called word blindness. There's a part of the brain that processes language, and another part of the brain that processes vision. If someone suffers brain damage to the area between the visual and language processing centers, they can lose the ability to read, without having severe impairments to other cognitive functions.

At some point someone became aware of children who had extreme problems with reading, with no apparent cause. This condition was termed congenital word blindness. It's been renamed dyslexia (difficulty with words). It used to be considered a rare condition, but now some snake oil salesman say 25% of the population have it (more reserved psychologists put the figure at 2%). There are rare forms of astigmatism that are often diagnosed as dyslexia. If someone suffers from such a form of astigmatism it can cause peculiar optical illusions, but the effects can sometimes be alleviated by reducing glare or improving lighting conditions.
